1.title: Introduction to Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and Transportation Systems
1.summary: Explores the historical evolution of mobility from walking and animal traction to modern high-speed transit. Introduces the definition of sustainable development from the Brundtland Report (1987), the 17 UN SDGs, and India's transportation profile.
key_takeaways: Walking is the primitive and most environmentally friendly mode of transport.
Sustainable development meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs (WCED, 1987).
Rio Earth Summit took place in Brazil in 1992, catalyzing Agenda 21.
The 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were established by the UN in 2015.
PURA (Provision of Urban Amenities to Rural Areas) was conceived by Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
Two-wheelers account for over 70% of registered motor vehicles in India.

2.title: Land-Use Plans, Zoning Schemes, and Baseline Environmental Impacts
2.summary: Details climate change drivers, greenhouse gases, and the multi-dimensional impacts of transport infrastructure on air, soil, water quality, human health, flora and fauna, and acoustic environments.
key_takeaways: Transport is responsible for nearly 23-25% of global energy-related CO2 emissions.
Psychological and physical wellbeing are interdependent; accident trauma causes both bodily injury and mental distress.
Primary transport air pollutants include PM2.5, PM10, NOx, CO, and non-methane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs).
Noise pollution above 65 dB(A) causes chronic cardiovascular stress and sleep disturbance.
Linear transport corridors cause severe habitat fragmentation, edge effects, and barrier effects on wildlife.

3.title: Urban & Regional Transport Planning and EIA Foundations
3.summary: Introduces Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) principles, administrative processes, screening, scoping, baseline surveys, and regulatory notifications in India under the MoEFCC.
key_takeaways: EIA was formally pioneered under the US National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) in 1969.
In India, EIA notifications were enacted in 1994 and revised comprehensively in 2006 under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
Category A projects require mandatory central environmental clearance by MoEFCC; Category B projects are handled by State SEIAA.
Scoping determines the specific Terms of Reference (TOR) for the Environmental Impact Assessment study.
Public hearings / consultations ensure stakeholder engagement and environmental justice before project clearance.

4.title: Global EIA Practices and Sectoral Case Studies
4.summary: Analyzes real-world EIA execution across diverse transport megaprojects including national expressways, dedicated freight railway corridors (DFC), international airports, and port terminals.
key_takeaways: Highways require dedicated animal underpasses and noise barriers through eco-sensitive zones.
Rail electrification dramatically lowers localized emissions compared to diesel traction corridors.
Greenfield airport EIAs focus heavily on noise contouring, bird-hit hazards, and stormwater runoff containment.
Port and terminal developments must assess marine dredging, siltation, ballast water treatment, and mangrove conservation.

5.title: Spatial Dynamics, Land Use Planning, and Transit-Oriented Development (TOD)
5.summary: Examines the reciprocal relationship between urban spatial structure and transportation. Focuses on master plans, zoning laws, and the principles of Transit Oriented Development (TOD).
key_takeaways: Land use determines trip generation patterns, while transport accessibility shapes land value and development density.
TOD centers around high-density, mixed-use communities located within a 5-10 minute walk (500–800 m) of transit stations.
The 3Ds of TOD: Density, Diversity, and Design (later expanded to 8 principles: Walk, Cycle, Connect, Transit, Mix, Densify, Compact, Shift).
Incentivized Floor Area Ratio (FAR) and reduced parking minimums encourage transit patronage.

6.title: TOD Case Studies and the 4-Step Traditional Planning Model
6.summary: Reviews TOD implementations across Delhi Metro, Belgrade, and Naya Raipur (Atal Nagar). Explains the traditional 4-step transport planning sequence alongside the modern Avoid-Shift-Improve (ASI) framework.
key_takeaways: Avoid-Shift-Improve (ASI) is the cornerstone paradigm of sustainable mobility.
The 4-Step Model: (1) Trip Generation, (2) Trip Distribution (e.g. Gravity Model), (3) Modal Split / Mode Choice (Logit model), (4) Traffic Assignment (User Equilibrium).
Traditional transport planning tended to be 'predict and provide', whereas sustainable planning is 'vision and validate'.
Naya Raipur was planned with dedicated BRT corridors and integrated non-motorized transport (NMT) spines.

7.title: Contemporary Planning, Travel Demand Management (TDM), and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)
7.summary: Explores Travel Demand Management (TDM) tools, activity-based modeling, and introduces the ISO 14040/14044 standard for Life Cycle Assessment across vehicular systems.
key_takeaways: TDM measures include congestion pricing (Singapore, London), high-occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes, and parking pricing.
LCA evaluates environmental burdens from 'cradle to grave' across all life stages.
Four mandatory LCA phases per ISO 14040: (1) Goal and Scope Definition, (2) Life Cycle Inventory (LCI), (3) Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA), (4) Interpretation.
The functional unit provides a reference to which all input and output flows are mathematically normalized (e.g., 1 passenger-km).

8.title: Material Flow Analysis (MFA), Circular Economy, and Transport Emissions Modelling
8.summary: Teaches Material Flow Analysis (MFA) based on the law of conservation of mass. Covers circular economy paradigms in the vehicle fleet and the basics of transport emissions inventory calculation.
key_takeaways: MFA is governed by the mass balance principle: Inputs = Outputs + Stock Changes (dm/dt = Σ m_in - Σ m_out).
Circular economy transitions from linear 'take-make-dispose' to closed loops (reduce, reuse, remanufacture, recycle).
End-of-life vehicle (ELV) recycling recovers valuable metals (steel, aluminium, copper, lithium, cobalt) and prevents hazardous leakage.
Emissions = Activity Data (vehicle-km travelled) × Emission Factor (g/km) × Fuel Consumption Factor.

9.title: Emissions Dispersion, Acoustic Modelling, and National Policies
9.summary: Covers line-source atmospheric dispersion (CALINE4, Gaussian plume models), traffic noise prediction models (CORTN), and key policy instruments including NUTP, NCAP, and BS-VI standards.
key_takeaways: CALINE4 is a Gaussian line-source dispersion model developed by Caltrans specifically for highway microenvironments.
Traffic noise decays at approximately 3 dB per doubling of distance for a line source over hard ground.
Bharat Stage VI (BS-VI) standards cut particulate matter emissions from diesel passenger vehicles by over 80% and NOx by 70%.
India's National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) targets 131 non-attainment cities to reduce particulate air pollution.

10.title: Decarbonization, Alternate Fuels, Electric Vehicles, and BRTS
10.summary: Investigates deep decarbonization strategies: alternate fuels (ethanol blending, CNG, LNG, green hydrogen), electric vehicle battery lifecycles, futuristic Hyperloop technology, and BRTS design.
key_takeaways: Electric vehicles eliminate tailpipe emissions, but overall sustainability depends on grid decarbonization (Well-to-Wheel analysis).
E20 represents 20% ethanol blended with petrol, targeted nationwide in India to displace imported crude.
Green hydrogen produced via renewable electrolysis offers zero-carbon heavy transport potential.
Hyperloop operates capsules in low-pressure evacuated tubes with magnetic levitation to eliminate rolling and aerodynamic resistance.
Ahmedabad Janmarg BRTS is an internationally recognized gold-standard BRT implementation in India.

11.title: Mass Transit, Green Airports, Waterways, NMT, and openLCA
11.summary: Examines sustainability innovations in Mass Rapid Transit (MRT regenerative braking), 100% solar airports (Cochin), Inland Waterways (NW-1), Complete Streets, and the openLCA open-source platform.
key_takeaways: Regenerative braking in metro trains feeds electrical energy back into the third rail/overhead traction catenary.
Cochin International Airport (CIAL) became the world's first fully solar-powered airport in 2015.
Inland Water Transport (IWT) consumes significantly less fuel per ton-km than road and rail haulage.
Complete Streets prioritize safe, equitable access for pedestrians, cyclists, motorists, and transit riders.
openLCA is a high-performance open-source LCA tool compatible with major databases like ecoinvent.

12.title: LCA Case Studies, STAN Tool, and Sustainability Indicators (DPSIR & STAR)
12.summary: Demonstrates practical modeling in openLCA and STAN (Substance Flow Analysis). Introduces DPSIR indicator frameworks, Multi-Criteria Analysis, and the Sustainable Transport Appraisal Rating (STAR).
key_takeaways: STAN software automates mass balancing, data reconciliation, and error propagation based on Austrian standard ÖNORM S 2096.
The DPSIR framework breaks down interactions into Driving forces (economic growth), Pressures (emissions), States (air quality), Impacts (health), and Responses (policy).
STAR (Sustainable Transport Appraisal Rating) uses Multi-Criteria Analysis (MCA) to evaluate project sustainability across economic, social, environmental, and engineering criteria.
Composite sustainability indices normalize, weight, and aggregate diverse indicators into a single actionable metric.

flashcards.front: What was the very first form of transportation for humans?
flashcards.back: Walking (primitive locomotion).

flashcards.front: Define Sustainable Development according to the Brundtland Commission (1987).
flashcards.back: Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

flashcards.front: In what year and where was the historic Earth Summit held?
flashcards.back: 1992 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

flashcards.front: How many Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were established by the United Nations?
flashcards.back: 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

flashcards.front: Who conceived the PURA (Provision of Urban Amenities to Rural Areas) development strategy in India?
flashcards.back: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, former President of India.

flashcards.front: Which vehicle category comprises the majority share (>70%) of total registered motor vehicles in India?
flashcards.back: Two-wheelers (motorcycles and scooters).

flashcards.front: What is the primary objective of Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)?
flashcards.back: To identify, predict, evaluate, and mitigate biophysical and social environmental effects of proposed development projects prior to major decisions.

flashcards.front: Name common methodologies used for EIA analysis.
flashcards.back: Ad-hoc methods, Checklists (simple, descriptive, scaling), Matrices (Leopold Matrix), Network diagrams, and GIS Overlays.

flashcards.front: Under which statutory act is EIA notified in India?
flashcards.back: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, notified by MoEFCC in 1994 and revised in 2006.

flashcards.front: What are the core '3Ds' of Transit Oriented Development (TOD)?
flashcards.back: Density, Diversity (mixed land use), and Design (pedestrian-friendly street network).

flashcards.front: What is the 'ASI' framework in sustainable mobility?
flashcards.back: Avoid/Reduce unnecessary motorized trips, Shift to green/public modes, and Improve vehicle & fuel energy efficiency.

flashcards.front: List the sequential steps in the traditional 4-Step Transportation Planning Model.
flashcards.back:
1. Trip Generation
2. Trip Distribution
3. Modal Split (Mode Choice)
4. Traffic Assignment

flashcards.front: What international standard governs Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)?
flashcards.back: ISO 14040 (Principles and framework) and ISO 14044 (Requirements and guidelines).

flashcards.front: What physical fundamental law forms the basis of Material Flow Analysis (MFA)?
flashcards.back: The Law of Conservation of Mass: Input = Output + Storage (Stock accumulation).

flashcards.front: What line-source dispersion model is commonly utilized for highway air quality analysis?
flashcards.back: CALINE4 (California Line Source Dispersion Model based on Gaussian plume theory).

flashcards.front: What is Well-to-Wheel (WTW) analysis?
flashcards.back: A life cycle assessment of vehicle fuels comprising Well-to-Tank (WTT, fuel production) and Tank-to-Wheel (TTW, vehicle operation).

flashcards.front: What are the fundamental engineering features of Hyperloop technology?
flashcards.back: Passenger capsules travelling inside low-pressure vacuum tubes utilizing magnetic levitation (Maglev) and linear induction propulsion.

flashcards.front: Which airport was certified as the world's first fully solar-powered green airport?
flashcards.back: Cochin International Airport (CIAL) in Kerala, India.

flashcards.front: What is STAN software used for, and which standard does it implement?
flashcards.back: SubSTance flow ANalysis (MFA software) implementing Austrian Standard ÖNORM S 2096.

flashcards.front: Explain the acronym DPSIR used in sustainability indicators.
flashcards.back: Driving forces → Pressures → State → Impacts → Responses.

glossary.desc: Formal process used to predict environmental consequences of a proposed development project before decision making.
Urban development maximizing residential, business and leisure space within walking distance of public transport.
Sustainable mobility framework: Avoid unnecessary travel, Shift to environmentally friendly modes, and Improve vehicle technology.
Methodology for assessing environmental impacts associated with all stages of the life cycle of a commercial product, process, or service (ISO 14040/14044).
Systematic assessment of the state and change of materials, stocks, and flows by mass balance within a defined system boundary.
Freeware supporting MFA according to Austrian standard ÖNORM S 2096, featuring data reconciliation and error propagation.
Open-source software application for Life Cycle Assessment and sustainability modeling developed by GreenDelta.

glossary.full: Driving force - Pressure - State - Impact - Response
glossary.desc: Causal framework for describing interactions between society and the environment adopted by the European Environment Agency.
Multicriteria appraisal framework evaluating transport projects across economic, social, environmental, and safeguard dimensions.
Application of strategies and policies to reduce travel demand, specifically that of single-occupancy private vehicles.
Bus-based public transport system designed to have higher capacity, speed, and reliability through dedicated right-of-way and off-board ticketing.
Comprehensive national framework launched in India (2019) aiming to achieve a 20-30% reduction in PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations across non-attainment cities.
Emission standards instituted by the Indian government mandating ultra-low sulfur (10 ppm) fuels and advanced aftertreatment systems (DPF, SCR).

glossary.full: Provision of Urban Amenities to Rural Areas
glossary.desc: Strategic rural-urban connectivity and sustainable development model proposed by former Indian President Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
Ratio of a building's total floor area to the size of the piece of land upon which it is built; key tool in transit-oriented zoning.
Life-cycle energy and emissions accounting from primary fuel extraction/generation to vehicle movement (Well-to-Tank + Tank-to-Wheel).
